etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English whale, from Old English hwæl (“whale”), from Proto-West Germanic *hwal, from Proto-Germanic *hwalaz (“whale”) (compare German Wal, Swedish val, Danish and Norwegian Bokmål hval, Norwegian Nynorsk kval; compare also Dutch walvis, West Frisian walfisk, from Proto-Indo-European *(s)kʷálos (“sheatfish”) (compare German Wels, Latin squalus (“big sea fish”), Old Prussian kalis, Ancient Greek ἄσπαλος (áspalos), Avestan 𐬐𐬀𐬭𐬀 (kara, “kind of fish”)).

definitions.definition: Any one of numerous large marine mammals comprising an informal group within infraorder Cetacea that usually excludes dolphins and porpoises.

definitions.definition: (finance, figuratively, informal) An investor who deals with very large amounts of money.

quote.text: The whale is still snoring. He's a real beauty, the whale. Got this thick curly hair all over his chest and stomach and legs.

etymologies.etymologyHTML: Uncertain. Perhaps a variant of wale influenced by whack, whap, etc.

definitions.definition: (slang, transitive) To thrash, to flog, to beat vigorously or soundly.

quote.text: Brought him back, put him in the stall—low stable—got out of his reach, and then begun to whale him. Then he kicked up agin;  […]

quote.citation: 1865 May, “Three Days at Camp Douglass”, in Our Young Folks: An Illustrated Magazine for Boys and Girls, volume I, number V, page 296:
quote.text: "I wouldn't let him. When you were a boy in your part of the country, and other boys told tales about you, what did you do with them?" "Whaled 'em like time, Captin'," answered the man; "and if ye'll only shet yer eyes to 't, I'll whale him." "I can't allow such things in the prison," said the Captain; "and besides, the fellow will be lame for a fortnight, and wouldn't be a match for you in that condition. Let him get limber, and then, if you don't whale him, I'll make you walk the ladder for a month." The result was, the conscript officer received a sound thrashing; and did not commit another act worthy of punishment for a week.
